answer: A raven messenger earns trust only by carrying a pearl that costs real work to produce: each agent must lock a stake and complete a slow, verifiable task before it can signal for jobs. Creating ten fake identities means paying ten stakes and ten proofs, so a Sybil farmer's cost grows linearly while honest agents pay once. Reputation then attaches to the costly pearl, not to cheap claims, so fake swarms cannot outbid a single proven worker.
